overview: Both sides fianchetto: 3...Bg7 4.Bg2 O-O 5.O-O d6, often with c4 and Nc3 added to reach a Fianchetto King's Indian. White keeps a flexible centre and may play c4, b3 or Nbd2; Black plays ...d6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5 or ...c5. Play is quiet and manoeuvring with little forced theory.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and add c4, Nc3 or b3 to pressure d5/e5.
Keep the centre flexible and avoid KID attacking lines.

black_ideas.idea: Wait for White to commit c4 before choosing the structure.

typical_structures.structure: Double fianchetto with flexible pawn centres; Fianchetto King's Indian after c4.

character.notes: Quiet, positional; neither side takes early risks.

approach.notes: A set-up White can play against most Black set-ups, but here named against the KID move order.

level.notes: Positional manoeuvres but no big theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Double Fianchetto
sublines_that_differ.how: White adds the queen's bishop on the long diagonal.

character.reason: Quiet manoeuvring, neither especially forcing nor hard to break.

approach.reason: Played by strong players, though it is a flexible set-up.

plans.reason: Both sides use fianchettoed bishops and indirect centre control.
